description:
Capture a snapshot of a page or spread from the active InDesign document. Returns the image as base64-encoded JPEG, rendered at the resolution a vision model can actually use (you do not set dpi).

Pass an optional `region` ([x0,y0,x1,y1], normalized 0..1 over the page) to zoom into part of a page at full detail — use this when a whole-page snapshot is too coarse to read an image or fine type. To capture one specific object by id, use `snapshot_object` instead.

Pass `preview: true` for a cheap low-resolution thumbnail — use it for quick 'did the layout roughly change / is the block where I dropped it' checks where you don't need to read detail. Omit it to read detail.

IMPORTANT: Use this tool only when YOU need to verify your work or when the user explicitly requests a snapshot. The user is viewing changes directly in InDesign - they do not need snapshots in the chat unless they ask for them.

description.description:
Brief description shown in the InDesign plugin panel. REQUIRED FORMAT:

Line 1: What Sidekick is doing (present progressive tense, e.g., 'Capturing page 1 for review')

Line 2: Manual alternative (e.g., 'You can also use **File > Export** (`Cmd+E`)')

ALWAYS include the manual alternative on line 2. Supports markdown: **bold**, `code`.

index.description: Zero-based index of the page or spread to capture

preview.description: Set true for a low-resolution thumbnail (~0.3 MP) for quick rough-glance checks where you don't need to read detail. Ignored when `region` is set (region always captures at full detail).

region.description: Optional zoom-box [x0,y0,x1,y1] in normalized 0..1 page coordinates (top-left origin). Omit to capture the whole page. Only valid with target 'page'. Example: [0.5,0,1,0.4] = top-right area.

target.description: Whether to capture a single page or an entire spread

name: snapshot
